header.title: Frontend Testing
header.description: Unit, Integration, and E2E Testing: Building a comprehensive testing strategy from scratch.

fundamentals.title: Testing Fundamentals
fundamentals.description: Understanding the three levels of testing and why they matter.

pyramid.title: The Testing Pyramid
pyramid.description: The testing pyramid illustrates the relationship between different types of tests. It emphasizes writing more unit tests, a moderate amount of integration tests, and fewer E2E tests.

whyPyramid.title: Why This Pyramid?
whyPyramid.unitTests: Unit Tests: Fast, cheap, and easy to write. Perfect for testing pure functions and isolated components.
whyPyramid.integrationTests: Integration Tests: Verify that different modules work together (e.g., API → state → UI).
whyPyramid.e2eTests: E2E Tests: Expensive and slow, but catch real-world scenarios. Use sparingly for critical paths.

unitTesting.title: Unit Testing
unitTesting.description: Unit tests isolate a single function or component and test it in isolation. They're the fastest and cheapest form of testing.

integrationTesting.title: Integration Testing
integrationTesting.description: Integration tests verify that multiple components and modules work together correctly. Typically, they test the full flow: API call → state update → UI render.

commonScenario.title: Common Integration Test Scenario
commonScenario.description: User clicks a button → Component makes API request → MSW intercepts and responds → Component updates state → New content appears on screen

e2eTesting.title: End-to-End (E2E) Testing
e2eTesting.description: E2E tests run in a real browser and simulate user actions. They're the slowest and most expensive, but they catch issues that unit and integration tests might miss.
e2eTesting.whenToUse: When to use E2E tests: Critical user journeys like login, checkout, or critical workflows. Avoid testing every interaction; focus on happy paths and key error cases.

testRatio.title: Test Ratio in Practice
testRatio.conclusion: This ratio ensures fast feedback (unit tests run instantly), reasonable coverage (integration tests catch real issues), and confidence in critical paths (E2E tests verify the whole system).

unitTesting.title: Unit Testing with React Testing Library
unitTesting.description: Testing React components the way users interact with them.

philosophy.title: React Testing Library Philosophy
philosophy.description: React Testing Library's guiding principle is: "Test the behavior, not the implementation." This means writing tests from the user's perspective, not based on how the component is coded.

corePhilosophy.title: Core Philosophy: User-Centric Testing
corePhilosophy.dontTestState: Don't test state: Users don't see state; they see rendered output
corePhilosophy.dontTestImplementation: Don't test implementation: How the component works shouldn't matter
corePhilosophy.testWhatUsersSee: Test what users see: Focus on DOM elements, buttons, text, and accessibility
corePhilosophy.simulateUserInteractions: Simulate user interactions: Click, type, submit forms

queries.title: Core Queries: getByRole
queries.description: The most recommended query is getByRole, as it aligns with how assistive technologies interact with the DOM. It also encourages semantic HTML.

userInteractions.title: User Interactions
userInteractions.description: Use userEvent (not fireEvent) to simulate user interactions. userEvent is more realistic and triggers all the events a real user would trigger.

comparison.title: userEvent vs fireEvent
comparison.userEvent: userEvent: Simulates real user behavior (setup(), click(), type(), etc.)
comparison.fireEvent: fireEvent: Directly triggers DOM events (older approach, less realistic)

asyncTesting.title: Async Testing Patterns
asyncTesting.description: Use findBy or waitFor when testing asynchronous operations like API calls.

integrationTesting.title: Integration Testing with MSW
integrationTesting.description: Testing component interactions with mocked API responses.

whatIsMSW.title: What is MSW?
whatIsMSW.description: Mock Service Worker (MSW) is a library that intercepts HTTP requests at the browser level and returns mock responses. It's perfect for testing how your components handle API calls without depending on a real backend.

whyMSW.title: Why MSW for Integration Tests?
whyMSW.noBackend: No backend dependency: Test frontend logic independently
whyMSW.realistic: Realistic scenarios: Simulate API errors, delays, and edge cases

whatIsMSW.flow: Flow: Component → fetch() → MSW intercepts → Mock response returned → Component updates UI

setup.title: Setting Up MSW in Tests
setup.description: Create a test setup file that initializes MSW handlers for your tests.

loadingSuccess.title: Testing Loading & Success States
loadingSuccess.description: Write tests that verify your component handles loading, success, and error states correctly.

errorScenarios.title: Testing Error Scenarios
errorScenarios.description: Override MSW handlers in specific tests to simulate API errors.

userInteractions.title: Testing User Interactions with API
userInteractions.description: Test the full flow: user action → API call → state update → UI change.

delays.title: Mocking Request Delays
delays.description: Simulate network delays to test loading states and timeouts.

guidelines.title: Integration Testing Guidelines
guidelines.happyPath: Test the happy path: Main user flow should work
guidelines.errorCases: Test error cases: API errors, network issues, timeouts
guidelines.edgeCases: Test edge cases: Empty states, large responses, slow networks
guidelines.useMSW: Use MSW: Mock APIs, not fetch directly
guidelines.dontMockComponents: Don't mock components: Test real component integration

vitest.title: Jest vs Vitest: Choosing Your Test Runner
vitest.description: Understanding the differences and when to use each.

jest.title: Jest: The Industry Standard
jest.description: Jest is the most widely used testing framework for JavaScript. It provides everything out-of-the-box: test runner, assertion library, mocking utilities, and coverage reporting.

strengths.title: Jest Strengths
strengths.mature: Mature ecosystem: Well-documented, tons of Stack Overflow answers
strengths.builtin: Built-in tools: No need for external libraries

weaknesses.title: Jest Weaknesses
weaknesses.slow: Slower: Transform overhead makes tests sometimes slow
weaknesses.complex: Complex configuration: Can require setup for modern tooling

vitest.title: Vitest: The Modern Alternative
vitest.description: Vitest is a modern testing framework built on Vite. It offers Jest-compatible APIs but with significantly better performance.

strengths.title: Vitest Strengths
strengths.fast: ⚡ Super fast: Leverages Vite's ES modules and instant HMR
strengths.modern: Modern tooling: Works seamlessly with modern build tools

setup.title: Setting Up Vitest
setup.description: If you're starting a new project with Vite, Vitest is the recommended choice.

migration.title: Migrating from Jest to Vitest
migration.description: Migration is usually straightforward since Vitest is Jest-compatible.

checklist.title: Migration Checklist
checklist.updatePackage: Update package.json: Change test script to use vitest
checklist.replaceJest: Replace jest.fn() with vi.fn(): Usually just import change
checklist.runTests: Run tests: Most should pass without changes

recommendation.title: Recommendation
recommendation.newProjects: For new projects: Use Vitest if you're already using Vite. You'll get better performance and faster feedback loops.
recommendation.existingProjects: For existing Jest projects: Keep Jest unless you're planning to migrate to Vite anyway. The effort isn't worth it for small projects.

e2e.title: End-to-End (E2E) Testing
e2e.description: Testing complete user journeys in a real browser environment.

whatIsE2E.title: What is E2E Testing?
whatIsE2E.description: End-to-End tests run your application in a real browser and simulate real user interactions. They test the complete flow from entry point to exit, catching issues that unit and integration tests might miss.

useCases.title: E2E Testing Use Cases
useCases.crossBrowser: Cross-browser compatibility: Ensure app works on Chrome, Firefox, Safari

whatIsE2E.warningDescription: E2E tests are slow and brittle because they depend on real browser behavior. Use them sparingly (5-10% of your test suite) for critical paths only.

playwright.title: Playwright: Enterprise-Grade Testing
playwright.description: Playwright is built by Microsoft and is optimized for modern web applications. It's fast, reliable, and CI-friendly.

strengths.title: Playwright Strengths
strengths.fast: ⚡ Fast: Optimized execution and parallel testing
strengths.crossBrowser: 🌐 Cross-browser: Chromium, Firefox, WebKit out of the box
strengths.dx: Developer experience: Great UI for debugging and recording tests

cypress.title: Cypress: Developer Experience Champion
cypress.description: Cypress prioritizes developer experience with an interactive interface, excellent debugging tools, and test recording.

strengths.title: Cypress Strengths
strengths.bestDX: 🎨 Best DX: Interactive test runner with visual feedback

limitations.title: Cypress Limitations
limitations.jsOnly: JavaScript only: Can't test multi-tab or mobile

guidelines.title: E2E Testing Guidelines
guidelines.criticalPaths: Test critical user paths: Login, checkout, core features
guidelines.avoidDetails: Avoid testing details: Don't test every button and input
guidelines.meaningfulWaits: Use meaningful waits: Wait for elements by role, not arbitrary delays
guidelines.keepIsolated: Keep tests isolated: Each test should be independent
guidelines.testData: Use test data carefully: Reset database between tests

ci.title: Running E2E Tests in CI
ci.description: Configure your CI/CD pipeline to run E2E tests on every push.

bestPractices.title: Mocking Strategies & Testing Antipatterns
bestPractices.description: How to mock effectively and avoid common testing pitfalls.

mockTypes.title: Types of Mocks
mockTypes.description: Mocking is essential for testing, but too much mocking can make tests unrealistic. Use mocks strategically.

summary.title: Mock Types Summary
summary.fn: vi.fn(): Create mock functions to track calls
summary.spy: vi.spyOn(): Spy on real functions without replacing them
summary.msw: MSW: Mock HTTP requests at the network level

doMockList.apis: External APIs and network requests (use MSW)
doMockList.slowOps: Slow operations (database, file system, crypto functions)
doMockList.sideEffects: Side effects you want to verify (analytics, logging)

dontMockList.unrealistic: Things that would make your test unrealistic

antipatterns.title: Testing Antipatterns to Avoid
antipatterns.description: Common mistakes that make tests brittle and unreliable.
antipatterns.correct2: CORRECT: Mock external dependencies, test real logic
antipatterns.correct4: CORRECT: Use findBy for async operations

goldenRules.title: Golden Rules of Mocking
goldenRules.boundary: Mock at the boundary: Mock network calls, file I/O, not business logic
goldenRules.keepSimple: Keep mocks simple: Complex mocks indicate complex dependencies
goldenRules.useMSW: Use MSW for HTTP: It's the most realistic way to mock APIs
goldenRules.testBehavior: Test behavior, not implementation: Change implementation without changing tests
goldenRules.resetMocks: Reset mocks between tests: Prevent test pollution

commonScenarios.title: Testing Common Scenarios
commonScenarios.description: Practical examples for common testing situations.

keepMaintainable.title: Keeping Tests Maintainable
keepMaintainable.oneConcept: One concept per test: Test should have a single assertion idea
keepMaintainable.clearNames: Clear test names: Describe what's being tested
keepMaintainable.reusableUtils: Reusable test utilities: Extract common test setup

strategy.title: Testing Strategy Summary
strategy.unitTests: 60-70% Unit Tests: Test pure functions and components in isolation
strategy.integrationTests: 20-30% Integration Tests: Use RTL + MSW to test component interactions
strategy.e2eTests: 5-10% E2E Tests: Use Playwright for critical user journeys
strategy.mockStrategically: Mock strategically: External APIs and slow operations only
strategy.testBehavior: Test behavior: Not implementation details or internals
